entry.title: 🧪 Testing in Production: The Rise of Shift-Right Testing in Modern QA
entry.summary: Testing is moving to production. This doesn’t mean abandoning pre-release testing. Instead, Shift-Right Testing complements it by adding real-world feedback, observability, and resilience validation directly in live environments. Let’s explore what it is, why it matters, and how teams are adopting it smartly. Shift-Right Testing is the practice of performing various types of tests after software is deployed to production. It flips the traditional mindset of “test first, deploy later” and embraces testing as a continuous activity. It includes: 🔁 Canary Releases 🧪 A/B Testing 🔍 Monitoring & Observability 🧯 Chaos Engineering 📊 User Behavior Analytics 📈 Real-World Feedback 🚀 Faster Release Cycles 🧠 Smarter Decision-Making 🛡️ Improved Resilience 1. Canary Deployments 2. Feature Flags 3. Real User Monitoring (RUM) 4. Synthetic Monitoring 5. Chaos Engineering Shift-Left = Prevent defects early (unit tests, integration tests, CI) Shift-Right = Detect hidden risks in production (user behavior, scalability, real-time issues) Smart teams don’t choose one — they blend both. While Shift-Right is powerful, it comes with its own set of risks: ⚠️ Need for proper rollback mechanisms 🔐 Must protect real user data and privacy 🧑‍💻 Requires buy-in from developers, ops, and product teams But with mature DevOps pipelines, observability tools, and cloud-native practices, these challenges are increasingly manageable. Software quality today isn’t a phase. It’s a lifecycle activity. From code commit to production user sessions, quality assurance needs to be baked into every step. And that’s what Shift-Right Testing enables — continuous confidence, not just gated approval. 🗣️ Are you already shifting right in your QA strategy? 💬 Share your thoughts and tools you use in production testing.

entry.title: DAY 8
entry.summary: Good Morning all! Today was a theory class and I learnt about some commonly used HTML semantic tags. Semantic tags are basically tags whose name itself provides a hint regarding the type of content present inside those. For example header tag indicates that it is the head of the document while the footer tag indicates the end of the document and so on. Some more semantic tags are article , aside , main , nav etc. Like I mentioned, the names of these tags itself indicates the type of content inside them. semantic tags is to improve our website's Search Engine Optimization(SEO) basically which means it way in which our website is indexed , crawled and ranked in a search engine's result page. So a really neat and ordered website with proper usage of these tags will help improve the website's indexing which in turn enables the website to reach more people. Okay so hope this helps those planning to build a website in the near future. That's all for today! See you guys tomorrow!
